perseus_medusa.title: Perseus and the Gorgon
perseus_medusa.summary: The hero Perseus is sent to bring back the head of Medusa, whose gaze turns flesh to stone. Guided by gifts from the gods, a mirrored shield, winged sandals, a cap of invisibility, he beheads her by looking only at her reflection, and from her severed neck springs the winged horse Pegasus.

theseus_minotaur.title: Theseus in the Labyrinth
theseus_minotaur.summary: Each year Athens sends youths to be devoured by the Minotaur in the Cretan Labyrinth. The hero Theseus volunteers, and with a thread given by Ariadne to mark his path, he slays the beast at the maze's heart and finds his way back out.

icarus_fall.title: The Fall of Icarus
icarus_fall.summary: The craftsman Daedalus fashions wings of feathers and wax to escape imprisonment, warning his son Icarus to fly neither too low nor too high. Intoxicated by flight, Icarus soars toward the sun; the wax melts, and he plunges into the sea.

ra_apep_nightly.title: Ra's Nightly Battle with Apep
ra_apep_nightly.summary: Every night the sun god Ra sails his barque through the underworld, and every night the great serpent Apep rises to swallow him and end the world. The gods defend the barque until dawn, when Ra emerges again; the eternal struggle explains the daily return of the sun.

weighing_heart.title: The Weighing of the Heart
weighing_heart.summary: The dead are led by Anubis to a hall where the heart is weighed against the feather of truth. A heart heavy with wrongdoing is devoured by the waiting beast Ammit, ending the soul forever; a light heart passes on into the afterlife.

enuma_elish.title: The Splitting of Tiamat
enuma_elish.summary: In the beginning the primordial dragon Tiamat gives birth to the gods, then turns to destroy them. The young god Marduk battles her, splits her vast body in two, and from the halves shapes the sky and the earth, ordering the cosmos from her remains.

gilgamesh_humbaba.title: Gilgamesh and the Guardian of the Forest
gilgamesh_humbaba.summary: The king Gilgamesh and his wild companion Enkidu journey to the sacred Cedar Forest to win everlasting fame. There they confront its terrible guardian Humbaba and slay him, an act of glory that sets in motion the grief and mortality at the heart of their story.

houyi_ten_suns.title: Houyi Shoots the Ten Suns
houyi_ten_suns.summary: Ten suns rise together and scorch the earth to cinders. The divine archer Houyi draws his bow and shoots down nine of them, leaving a single sun to warm the world, and is rewarded with the elixir of immortality that drives the later legend of the moon.

nuwa_mends_sky.title: Nuwa Mends the Sky
nuwa_mends_sky.summary: When a catastrophe tears a hole in the heavens and fire and flood pour through, the serpent-bodied goddess Nuwa smelts stones of five colors to patch the sky and cuts the legs from a great turtle to prop up its four corners, saving humanity she herself had made.

amaterasu_cave.title: Amaterasu and the Cave
amaterasu_cave.summary: Insulted by her brother, the sun goddess Amaterasu hides in a cave and the world falls dark. The gods gather outside and stage a raucous dance; curious at the laughter, she peers out, catches her own radiance in a mirror, and light returns to the world.

binding_fenrir.title: The Binding of Fenrir
binding_fenrir.summary: The gods raise the wolf Fenrir but come to fear the doom he will bring. They trick him into being bound by a ribbon forged from impossible things; sensing betrayal, he demands a hand in his jaws as surety, and the god Tyr pays that price to chain him until the end of the world.

thor_midgard.title: Thor and the World Serpent
thor_midgard.summary: The thunder god Thor goes fishing with a giant and hooks Jörmungandr, the serpent that circles the world. He hauls the monster to the surface in a contest of raw strength, a meeting the myths promise will come again at Ragnarök, where the two are fated to kill each other.

la_llorona_drowning.title: The Weeping Woman
la_llorona_drowning.summary: A woman drowns her own children in a river, in grief or in rage, then dies wretched on its banks. Now her spirit wanders the water's edge at night, weeping and searching, and parents warn that she will take any child who strays near the river after dark.

quetzalcoatl_exile.title: The Fall of Quetzalcoatl
quetzalcoatl_exile.summary: The feathered serpent Quetzalcoatl rules a golden age until he is shamed and driven from his city. He departs eastward over the sea on a raft of serpents, promising one day to return, a promise that echoed through later history.

strigoi_return.title: The Return of the Strigoi
strigoi_return.summary: A troubled soul refuses to rest and rises from the grave as a strigoi, returning to drain the vitality of its own family and village. The dead is exhumed and its heart pierced or burned so it will lie still, a folk practice that fed the later vampire legend.

baba_yaga_hut.title: Baba Yaga and the Hut on Hen's Legs
baba_yaga_hut.summary: A child sent into the forest comes upon a hut that turns on giant chicken legs, home to the witch Baba Yaga, who flies in a mortar. She sets impossible tasks and may devour or may reward; the clever and the kind survive her, the cruel do not.

koschei_death.title: Koschei the Deathless
koschei_death.summary: The sorcerer Koschei cannot be killed, for he has hidden his death away: a needle inside an egg, inside a duck, inside a hare, inside a chest, buried beneath an island oak. Only by unwinding this nesting secret can a hero end him and free the stolen bride.

banshee_cry.title: The Cry of the Banshee
banshee_cry.summary: By night a wailing is heard outside a house, keening and inconsolable. It is the banshee, whose cry belongs to certain old families, and those who hear her know that a death among them is already near.

selkie_wife.title: The Selkie Wife
selkie_wife.summary: A fisherman finds a sealskin on the shore and hides it, taking the selkie woman it belongs to as his wife. She lives with him and bears his children, but always watches the sea; the day she finds her skin, she slips it on and returns to the waves forever.

rainbow_serpent_shaping.title: The Rainbow Serpent Shapes the Land
rainbow_serpent_shaping.summary: In the Dreaming, the great Rainbow Serpent moves across a formless land, and where it winds the rivers and gorges are carved, the waterholes filled, the ranges raised. It remains in the deep water as a giver of life and rain, honored across many Aboriginal nations.

maui_taniwha.title: The Guardian in the Water
maui_taniwha.summary: A taniwha dwells in a river or harbor as its guardian, sometimes protecting a people and their canoes, sometimes demanding respect through danger. Māori tradition tells of many taniwha by name, each bound to a specific water and its community.

mothman_bridge.title: The Mothman and the Bridge
mothman_bridge.summary: For a year a red-eyed winged figure is seen around a West Virginia town, glimpsed on lonely roads and at an old munitions site. The sightings end when the town's Silver Bridge collapses into the river, and the creature passes into legend as a herald of the disaster.

bell_witch_haunting.title: The Bell Witch
bell_witch_haunting.summary: A Tennessee farm family is tormented for years by an unseen voice that speaks, sings, and strikes in the dark, seeming to know everything about them. The haunting becomes one of America's most famous, said even to have frightened a future president away.

wendigo_hunger.title: The Wendigo's Hunger
wendigo_hunger.summary: In the frozen northern woods, a person who turns to cannibalism to survive the winter is said to become a wendigo, gaunt and insatiable, its hunger growing with every meal. The tale warns against greed and the loss of one's humanity to want.

yeti_snows.title: The Yeti of the High Snows
yeti_snows.summary: High on the Himalayan passes, travelers and villagers tell of an ape-like figure moving through the snow above the tree line, glimpsed at a distance and known by its tracks. Sacred to some mountain communities, it endures as the most famous of the world's wild-man legends.

krampus_night.title: Krampusnacht
krampus_night.summary: On the eve of St. Nicholas, while the saint rewards good children, his horned companion Krampus comes for the wicked, rattling chains and switches and threatening to carry the worst away in his basket. Alpine towns still parade the beast through the winter streets.

prometheus_fire.title: Prometheus Steals Fire
prometheus_fire.summary: The Titan Prometheus takes pity on cold, helpless humankind and steals fire from the gods to give them warmth, craft, and civilization. For this defiance Zeus chains him to a rock where an eagle devours his liver each day, only for it to regrow each night, an eternal punishment for the gift of progress.

pandora_jar.title: Pandora's Jar
pandora_jar.summary: The gods fashion the first woman, Pandora, and send her to earth with a sealed jar she is told never to open. Overcome by curiosity, she lifts the lid and releases every sorrow, sickness, and hardship into the world; only Hope remains caught inside when she closes it again.

orpheus_underworld.title: Orpheus and Eurydice
orpheus_underworld.summary: The musician Orpheus descends into the underworld to reclaim his dead wife Eurydice, his playing so beautiful that the lords of death relent, on one condition: he must not look back at her until both reach the light. At the last step he turns, and she is lost to him forever.

heracles_labors.title: The Twelve Labors of Heracles
heracles_labors.summary: To atone for a madness sent by a jealous goddess, the strongman Heracles must complete twelve impossible tasks: strangling the Nemean lion, slaying the many-headed Hydra, capturing the hound of the underworld, and more. Each labor becomes a legend, and together they make him the greatest of Greek heroes.

theseus_ariadne.title: Theseus and the Thread
theseus_ariadne.summary: Sent as tribute to the Minotaur's Labyrinth, the Athenian prince Theseus wins the love of Ariadne, who gives him a ball of thread to unwind as he goes. He slays the beast at the maze's heart and follows the thread back to daylight, though his triumph carries a bitter cost.

bellerophon_chimera.title: Bellerophon and the Chimera
bellerophon_chimera.summary: Riding the winged horse Pegasus, the hero Bellerophon is sent to kill the Chimera, a fire-breathing blend of lion, goat, and serpent. From the air he defeats the monster, but later pride leads him to fly toward the home of the gods, and he falls.

persephone_seasons.title: The Abduction of Persephone
persephone_seasons.summary: Hades seizes the maiden Persephone and carries her to the underworld. Her mother Demeter, goddess of grain, mourns so deeply the earth goes barren, until a bargain is struck: Persephone spends part of the year below and part above, and her return each spring brings the world back to life.

daedalus_icarus2.title: Daedalus and the Labyrinth
daedalus_icarus2.summary: The master craftsman Daedalus builds the great Labyrinth to hold the Minotaur, so cunning a maze that he himself can barely escape it. Imprisoned by the king who fears his secrets, he devises wings of wax and feather to fly to freedom, a genius that saves and dooms in equal measure.

odysseus_return.title: The Wanderings of Odysseus
odysseus_return.summary: After the fall of Troy, the clever king Odysseus spends ten years fighting his way home across a sea of monsters: the one-eyed Cyclops, the song of the Sirens, the whirlpool Charybdis and the six-headed Scylla. His wit, more than his sword, carries him back to his waiting wife.

narcissus_echo.title: Narcissus and Echo
narcissus_echo.summary: The beautiful youth Narcissus scorns all who love him, including the nymph Echo, cursed to repeat only others' words. In punishment he falls in love with his own reflection in a pool and, unable to leave it, wastes away, becoming the flower that bears his name.

samudra_manthan.title: The Churning of the Ocean
samudra_manthan.summary: Gods and demons together churn the cosmic ocean of milk, using a mountain as the churning-rod and the great serpent as the rope. From the waters rise treasures, a deadly poison one god swallows to save creation, and at last the nectar of immortality, over which gods and demons war.

ramayana_rescue.title: Rama and the Rescue of Sita
ramayana_rescue.summary: The exiled prince Rama's wife Sita is carried off by the ten-headed demon-king Ravana. With an army of bears and the devoted monkey-hero Hanuman, Rama crosses to the demon's island fortress, wages a great war, and wins her back, the triumph of duty and devotion over pride.

indra_vritra.title: Indra Slays Vritra
indra_vritra.summary: The serpent-dragon Vritra coils around the mountains and holds back all the world's waters, bringing drought and death. The storm-god Indra, fortified and armed with a thunderbolt, shatters the dragon and releases the rivers to flow, restoring life to a parched creation.

garuda_nectar.title: Garuda and the Stolen Nectar
garuda_nectar.summary: To free his enslaved mother, the mighty eagle Garuda flies to seize the gods' nectar of immortality, battling past fire and guardians to take it. He wins his mother's freedom through the deed, and becomes the divine mount of Vishnu and the eternal foe of serpents.

krishna_govardhan.title: Krishna Lifts the Mountain
krishna_govardhan.summary: When a village faces the wrath of a storm-god's endless rain, the young Krishna lifts an entire mountain on one finger to shelter the people and their herds beneath it. For seven days he holds it, humbling the proud god and revealing his own divinity.

mahabharata_war.title: The War of Kurukshetra
mahabharata_war.summary: Two branches of a royal family, cousins raised as brothers, fall into a dispute over the throne that no council can settle. It erupts into a vast and tragic war on the field of Kurukshetra, where duty, family, and righteousness are torn apart, and a god counsels a wavering prince on the meaning of it all.

osiris_death.title: The Death and Rebirth of Osiris
osiris_death.summary: The good king Osiris is murdered and dismembered by his jealous brother Set, who scatters the pieces across the land. His wife Isis gathers them, binds them, and revives him long enough to conceive a son; Osiris then becomes lord of the dead, and his rebirth mirrors the flooding Nile.

horus_set.title: The Contendings of Horus and Set
horus_set.summary: Horus, son of the murdered Osiris, contests his uncle Set for the throne of Egypt in a long series of trials, battles, and cunning tricks judged by the gods. Horus at last prevails, restoring order after chaos, and every living pharaoh is called his living image.

isis_name_ra.title: Isis and the Secret Name of Ra
isis_name_ra.summary: The clever goddess Isis fashions a serpent to poison the aging sun-god Ra, then offers to heal him, but only if he tells her his hidden, true name, the source of all his power. In agony he yields it, and with that secret Isis gains magic to rival the greatest of gods.

gilgamesh_flood.title: Gilgamesh and the Flood
gilgamesh_flood.summary: Grieving his dead friend and terrified of death, the king Gilgamesh journeys to the one man granted immortality, who tells him of a great flood the gods once sent to drown the world, and of the ark that survived it. Gilgamesh learns he cannot escape death, only live well within it.

inanna_descent.title: The Descent of Inanna
inanna_descent.summary: The goddess Inanna descends into the underworld ruled by her sister, passing through seven gates and surrendering a garment at each until she stands stripped and is struck dead. Rescued by cunning, she may return only if another takes her place, a bargain that sets the seasons turning.

death_baldr.title: The Death of Baldr
death_baldr.summary: The beloved god Baldr dreams of his death, so his mother makes every thing in the world swear never to harm him, all but the harmless mistletoe. The trickster Loki guides a blind god's hand to throw a mistletoe dart, and Baldr falls, the first shadow of the doom to come.

theft_mjolnir.title: The Theft of Thor's Hammer
theft_mjolnir.summary: When a giant steals Thor's hammer and demands a goddess as ransom, the gods dress Thor himself as the bride. At the wedding feast the disguised thunder-god waits until his hammer is laid in his lap, then seizes it and turns the hall to ruin.

ragnarok.title: Ragnarök
ragnarok.summary: The myths foretell the end: a great winter, the breaking of chains, the wolf Fenrir loosed, the world-serpent rising, and the gods marching to a last battle in which most of them fall. The world burns and sinks, then rises green again from the sea, and life begins anew.

pangu_creation.title: Pangu Separates Heaven and Earth
pangu_creation.summary: From a cosmic egg the giant Pangu awakes and pushes the murky chaos apart, holding sky above and earth below as he grows for eighteen thousand years. When at last he dies, his breath becomes the wind, his eyes the sun and moon, and his body the mountains and rivers of the world.

journey_west.title: The Monkey King's Rebellion
journey_west.summary: Born from stone and mastering magic, the Monkey King Sun Wukong grows so mighty he storms heaven itself and must be pinned beneath a mountain. Freed to escort a monk on a pilgrimage west, he battles demons across a thousand trials on the road to redemption.

weaver_cowherd.title: The Weaver Girl and the Cowherd
weaver_cowherd.summary: A mortal cowherd and a heavenly weaving-maiden fall in love and marry, angering the gods who separate them across a great river of stars. Once a year magpies form a bridge so the two may meet for a single night, a tale still marked by a summer festival.

izanagi_izanami.title: Izanagi and Izanami
izanagi_izanami.summary: The divine pair Izanagi and Izanami stir the sea with a jeweled spear and create the islands of Japan, then birth its gods. When Izanami dies, Izanagi follows her into the land of the dead, but breaks his promise not to look and must flee her decay, sealing the border between life and death.

susanoo_orochi.title: Susanoo Slays the Eight-Headed Serpent
susanoo_orochi.summary: Exiled from heaven, the storm-god Susanoo finds a family mourning a daughter to be devoured by the eight-headed serpent Orochi. He fills eight vats with sake, and when the drunken serpent sleeps, he hews off each head, finding in its tail a great sword he offers to his sister the sun.

urashima_taro.title: Urashima Taro
urashima_taro.summary: A kind fisherman rescues a turtle and is carried to a palace beneath the sea, where he lives in bliss for what seems days. Returning home with a forbidden box, he finds a hundred years have passed; he opens the box in despair and the lost years fall upon him at once.

cu_chulainn.title: The Hound of Ulster
cu_chulainn.summary: A boy kills the fierce guard-dog of the smith Culann and pledges to take its place, earning the name Cú Chulainn. He grows into Ulster's greatest warrior, seized in battle by a terrible frenzy, and single-handedly holds the province against an invading army in his short, blazing life.

children_lir.title: The Children of Lir
children_lir.summary: A jealous stepmother turns the four children of Lir into swans, cursed to wander the cold lakes and seas of Ireland for nine hundred years, keeping only their voices and their love for one another. When the spell finally breaks, they crumble at once into great age.

finn_salmon.title: Finn and the Salmon of Knowledge
finn_salmon.summary: A young Finn is set to cook the Salmon of Knowledge, which grants all wisdom to whoever first tastes it. Burning his thumb on the fish, he sucks it to ease the pain and the wisdom passes to him; thereafter he need only bite his thumb to know what he must.

sword_stone.title: The Sword in the Stone
sword_stone.summary: A sword stands fixed in a stone, and it is foretold that only the true king of Britain can draw it free. Where mighty knights fail, a boy named Arthur lifts it without effort, and a squire becomes a king, beginning the age of Camelot.

holy_grail.title: The Quest for the Grail
holy_grail.summary: Arthur's knights scatter across the land in search of the Holy Grail, the vessel of miracles glimpsed in a vision at the Round Table. The quest tests each knight's worth and purity, and only the most blameless is granted to look upon what all the rest have sought in vain.

pied_piper.title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin
pied_piper.summary: A piper in colorful dress rids the town of Hamelin of its rats with an enchanting tune, but when the townsfolk refuse to pay, he pipes again, and this time it is their children who follow him out of the town, never to be seen again.

lorelei_rock.title: The Lorelei
lorelei_rock.summary: On a great rock above the Rhine sits a golden-haired maiden whose song drifts over the water. Boatmen who look up to find her lose their course in the current below and are dashed against the rocks, drawn to their deaths by her unearthly, sorrowful singing.

faust_bargain.title: The Bargain of Faust
faust_bargain.summary: The scholar Faust, hungry for knowledge and pleasure beyond human limits, strikes a bargain with a devil: earthly power and every desire, in exchange for his soul. The legend of his brilliant, damned life became the West's great parable of ambition without end.

melusine_secret.title: The Secret of Melusine
melusine_secret.summary: A lord weds the beautiful Melusine on her single condition: he must never look upon her on a Saturday. She brings him fortune and heirs, but at last he spies her bathing and sees her serpent's tail; discovered, she cries out and flies from the castle forever.

el_dorado.title: The Search for El Dorado
el_dorado.summary: Spanish explorers hear of a king so rich he powders his body in gold dust and washes it off in a sacred lake, and of a city of gold hidden in the New World's interior. The dream of El Dorado lures expedition after expedition to ruin in the mountains and jungles.

firebird.title: The Firebird
firebird.summary: A prince who catches a single glowing feather of the Firebird is sent to capture the bird itself, and then to win a horse, and then a princess, each impossible task leading to the next. With the help of a grey wolf he wins them all, and the radiant bird rewards the pure of heart.

vasilisa.title: Vasilisa the Beautiful
vasilisa.summary: Sent by a cruel stepmother into the forest to fetch fire from the witch Baba Yaga, the gentle Vasilisa survives only through the help of a magic doll her mother left her. She completes the witch's deadly tasks and returns with a skull of fire that destroys those who wronged her.

sampo_forging.title: The Forging of the Sampo
sampo_forging.summary: In the Finnish epic, the smith Ilmarinen forges the Sampo, a magical mill that grinds out grain, salt, and gold without end, as the price of a bride. The wondrous object brings prosperity and then war, as heroes battle over it until it shatters into the sea.

romulus_remus.title: Romulus and Remus
romulus_remus.summary: Twin brothers, cast out as infants and suckled by a she-wolf, grow up to found a city on the hills where they were saved. In a quarrel over its walls Romulus kills Remus and names the city Rome after himself, staining its birth with a brother's blood.

aeneas_journey.title: The Voyage of Aeneas
aeneas_journey.summary: Fleeing the burning ruins of Troy, the hero Aeneas carries his father and his gods across the sea toward a promised land in Italy. Through storm, love, and war he presses on, fated to father the line that will one day raise Rome.

rostam_sohrab.title: Rostam and Sohrab
rostam_sohrab.summary: The great Persian champion Rostam meets a young enemy warrior of unmatched courage on the battlefield and, after two days of struggle, kills him, only to find on the youth's arm the token he once gave the boy's mother. He has slain his own son, Sohrab, and grief undoes him.

jamshid_reign.title: The Reign of Jamshid
jamshid_reign.summary: The ancient king Jamshid teaches humanity to forge weapons, weave cloth, and build, ushering in a golden age of peace and plenty. But grown proud, he claims to be divine, and his glory abandons him, opening the way for the serpent-shouldered tyrant Zahhak.

simurgh_zal.title: The Simurgh and Zal
simurgh_zal.summary: A white-haired infant is abandoned on a mountain and raised by the great benevolent bird Simurgh, who nurtures him into the noble warrior Zal. When he returns to the world of men, the Simurgh gives him a feather to burn in any hour of need, and her wisdom guides his line.

thousand_nights.title: A Thousand and One Nights
thousand_nights.summary: To stay her execution, the clever Scheherazade tells the king a story each night and breaks it off at dawn, so he must spare her to hear the end. Across a thousand nights she spins the tales of Aladdin, Sinbad, and Ali Baba, until her wit wins both her life and his heart.

anansi_stories.title: Anansi and the Sky-God's Stories
anansi_stories.summary: The spider Anansi wishes to own all the world's stories, kept by the sky-god, who names an impossible price: to capture a python, a leopard, hornets, and an unseen spirit. By cleverness rather than strength Anansi delivers them all, and the stories become his, and ours.

sundiata.title: Sundiata, the Lion King of Mali
sundiata.summary: A prince born unable to walk is mocked and exiled, but rises on iron rods to his feet and grows into a mighty king. Sundiata returns from exile to defeat a sorcerer-king and found the great empire of Mali, and griots sing his deeds to this day.

kebra_negast.title: The Queen of Sheba and the Lion's Line
kebra_negast.summary: The Queen of Sheba journeys to the court of a wise king, and from their meeting is born a son who founds a royal line said to endure for three thousand years. The tale binds a nation's kings to the glory of the ancient story.

popol_vuh.title: The Hero Twins of the Popol Vuh
popol_vuh.summary: Two brothers, master ballplayers, are summoned to the underworld by its lords and made to endure deadly houses of knives, cold, and fire. Through cunning and self-sacrifice they defeat death itself, then rise into the sky to become the sun and the moon.

fifth_sun.title: The Legend of the Fifth Sun
fifth_sun.summary: The world has been created and destroyed four times, and to raise a fifth sun the gods gather in darkness and one must leap into a great fire. A humble, sickly god throws himself in first and rises as the sun, and the age we live in begins with that sacrifice.

inca_origin.title: Manco Cápac and the Founding of Cusco
inca_origin.summary: The sun-god sends his children from the waters of Lake Titicaca with a golden staff, telling them to found a city where it sinks into the earth. Where the staff vanishes they raise Cusco, and the first Inca teaches the people to farm, weave, and worship the sun.

guarani_creation.title: The Twins and the Jaguar
guarani_creation.summary: In Guaraní tradition, twin brothers born of tragedy wander a young world, outwitting the jaguars who killed their mother and setting the order of things. Their deeds explain the sun and moon and the shape of the land the people know.

maui_sun.title: Maui Snares the Sun
maui_sun.summary: The days are too short, so the demigod Maui and his brothers plait ropes and lie in wait at the pit where the sun rises. They snare it as it climbs and beat it until it swears to move more slowly across the sky, giving the world its long, workable days.

maui_fish.title: Maui Fishes Up the Land
maui_fish.summary: With a hook made from a jawbone and his own blood for bait, the demigod Maui casts into the deep sea and hauls up a vast fish, which becomes the land itself. His brothers hack at it greedily before it is blessed, and so the island's mountains and valleys are carved.

ramakien.title: The Ramakien
ramakien.summary: In the Thai telling of a great epic, the noble Rama, aided by the white monkey-general Hanuman, wars against the ten-necked demon king who has stolen his queen. The story fills temple walls and shadow-plays, a national retelling of duty, loyalty, and the fall of pride.

hang_tuah.title: Hang Tuah the Warrior
hang_tuah.summary: The peerless Malay warrior Hang Tuah serves his sultan with absolute loyalty, so absolute that when he is wrongly condemned and his best friend rebels in protest, Hang Tuah is sent to kill him. Their duel is the tragic heart of the Malay world's greatest legend.

jason_argonauts.title: Jason and the Golden Fleece
jason_argonauts.summary: The prince Jason gathers the greatest heroes of the age aboard the Argo to win the Golden Fleece, guarded by a sleepless dragon in a distant land. With the sorceress Medea's help he takes it, but their tangled love turns to one of myth's darkest betrayals.

sisyphus.title: The Boulder of Sisyphus
sisyphus.summary: For cheating death twice, the crafty king Sisyphus is condemned in the underworld to roll a great boulder up a hill, only for it to roll back down each time he nears the top. His endless, futile labor became the image of struggle without reward.

volsung_sigurd.title: Sigurd and the Dragon Fafnir
volsung_sigurd.summary: The young hero Sigurd is set to slay Fafnir, a man turned by greed into a hoard-guarding dragon. He digs a pit, pierces the beast from below, and tasting its blood gains the speech of birds, who warn him of the treachery coiled around the cursed gold.

saga_grettir.title: Grettir and the Draugr
saga_grettir.summary: The mighty outlaw Grettir wrestles the walking-dead draugr Glámr in a haunted farmstead, breaking the creature at last. But as it dies the draugr curses him with a fear of the dark, and the strongest man in Iceland is undone not by any foe but by dread.

wanda_vistula.title: Queen Wanda and the Vistula
wanda_vistula.summary: The beloved Polish queen Wanda refuses a foreign prince's hand and his war, and rather than let her people suffer for her sake, she gives herself to the river Vistula. Her sacrifice saves the kingdom, and her name lingers on its banks.

marko_kraljevic.title: Prince Marko
marko_kraljevic.summary: In South Slavic song the mighty Prince Marko rides his talking horse Šarac and rights wrongs across a land under foreign rule, his enormous strength matched by a rough sense of justice. He becomes the people's champion, half history and half legend.

white_stag.title: The Wondrous Stag
white_stag.summary: Two brothers, Hunor and Magor, chase a shining white stag that leads them ever onward into a new and fertile land, then vanishes. There they settle and father two nations, and the miraculous hunt becomes the origin tale of a people.

etana_eagle.title: Etana and the Eagle
etana_eagle.summary: The childless king Etana befriends an eagle and rides upon its back high into the heavens in search of the plant of birth that will give him an heir. The dizzying flight, where the earth shrinks to nothing below, is one of the oldest images of human ascent.

savitri_satyavan.title: Savitri and the Lord of Death
savitri_satyavan.summary: When Death comes to claim her husband, the devoted Savitri follows and walks beside him, answering his riddles with such wisdom that he grants her boon after boon, until she cleverly asks for her husband's life restored. Her devotion outwits death itself.

ganesha_head.title: How Ganesha Got His Head
ganesha_head.summary: Set to guard his mother's door, a boy refuses entry to a stranger who is in truth the god Shiva, who strikes off the boy's head in anger. To console the grieving mother, Shiva replaces it with the head of an elephant, and so the beloved remover of obstacles is born.

white_snake.title: The Legend of the White Snake
white_snake.summary: A white snake spirit takes the form of a woman and falls in love with a mortal man, living happily until a meddling monk exposes her nature and imprisons her beneath a pagoda. The tale of love across the border of human and spirit is among China's most cherished.

chang_e.title: Chang'e Flies to the Moon
chang_e.summary: When the archer Houyi wins the elixir of immortality, his wife Chang'e drinks it, whether to save it from a thief or by longing, and floats up to live forever on the cold moon. There she remains with a jade rabbit, honored each autumn at the mid-harvest festival.

dangun.title: Dangun and the Founding of Korea
dangun.summary: A bear and a tiger beg to become human; the bear endures a hundred days in a cave on garlic and mugwort and is transformed into a woman, who bears a son to the son of heaven. That son, Dangun, founds the first Korean kingdom.

shim_cheong.title: The Filial Daughter Shim Cheong
shim_cheong.summary: To restore her blind father's sight, the devoted Shim Cheong sells herself as a sacrifice to the sea. Her purity so moves the sea-king that she is returned to the world inside a lotus, becomes a queen, and is reunited with her father, whose eyes open at the sound of her voice.

lac_long_quan.title: The Dragon Lord and the Mountain Fairy
lac_long_quan.summary: The dragon-lord of the sea weds a mountain fairy, and she bears a sac of a hundred eggs that hatch a hundred children. The two part, fifty following the father to the coast and fifty the mother to the highlands, becoming the ancestors of the Vietnamese people.

malakas_maganda.title: Malakas and Maganda
malakas_maganda.summary: A great bird, weary of the endless sea and sky, cracks open a floating bamboo from which step the first man and woman, Malakas the Strong and Maganda the Beautiful. From them the islands' people descend, in a creation told across the Philippines.

nyai_roro_kidul.title: Nyai Roro Kidul, Queen of the Southern Sea
nyai_roro_kidul.summary: The spirit-queen of the southern ocean rules the waves off Java, beautiful and perilous, said to claim those who wear her forbidden green into the surf. Kings once wed her by legend to secure their power, and the sea still belongs to her.

tiddalik.title: Tiddalik the Flood-Frog
tiddalik.summary: A giant frog drinks every drop of water in the land, and the parched animals must make him laugh to release it. One by one they try and fail, until a dancing eel's antics break his solemn face, and the flood of his laughter fills the rivers again.

pele_volcano.title: Pele, Goddess of the Volcano
pele_volcano.summary: The fire-goddess Pele journeys down the island chain, digging her fiery home into each land only to be driven on, until she settles in the great crater of Hawaii. Her furies are the eruptions and lava flows, and she walks among people still, testing their kindness.

raven_light.title: Raven Steals the Light
raven_light.summary: In a world kept in darkness by a selfish chief who hoards the sun, moon, and stars, the trickster Raven transforms himself to slip into the chief's house and carry off the light, releasing it into the sky. The Pacific Northwest's great trickster gives the world its day.

anansi_caribbean.title: Anansi Crosses the Water
anansi_caribbean.summary: Carried across the ocean in the memories of the enslaved, the spider Anansi becomes the Caribbean's cunning hero, winning by wit what he cannot by force and turning the powerful into fools. His survival is itself the story: the trickster who could not be taken.

flying_dutchman.title: The Flying Dutchman
flying_dutchman.summary: A sea captain, cursed for his defiance in a great storm, is doomed to sail the oceans forever, never making port. Sailors who glimpse the spectral ship glowing on the horizon read it as an omen of doom, a legend that spread across every seafaring nation.

golem_prague.title: The Golem of Prague
golem_prague.summary: To protect his people, a rabbi of Prague shapes a giant from river clay and animates it with a holy word set in its mouth. The Golem guards the community faithfully until it grows uncontrollable, and the rabbi must unmake it, laying its clay to rest in an attic.

dracula_legend.title: The Legend of the Blood-Count
dracula_legend.summary: From the folklore of the undead strigoi and a cruel medieval prince grew the legend of a deathless count who sleeps by day and drinks the blood of the living by night. Rooted in Transylvanian soil, the tale became the modern world's defining vampire story.

nibelungenlied.title: The Song of the Nibelungs
nibelungenlied.summary: Siegfried, bathed invulnerable in dragon’s blood but for one leaf-covered spot, wins a hoard and a bride before he is murdered at a spring. His widow Kriemhild spends the rest of the epic exacting a revenge that consumes an entire court.

tannhauser.title: Tannhäuser in the Venusberg
tannhauser.summary: A knight discovers the hidden mountain hall of Venus and spends a year in its pleasures. Stricken with remorse he seeks absolution in Rome, is told he will be forgiven only when the Pope’s staff sprouts leaves, and turns away in despair three days before it flowers.

lohengrin.title: The Knight of the Swan
lohengrin.summary: A knight arrives in a boat drawn by a swan to champion a wronged duchess, on one condition: she must never ask his name or where he comes from. She asks, and the swan returns to carry him away forever.

barbarossa_sleeps.title: Barbarossa Beneath the Mountain
barbarossa_sleeps.summary: The emperor is not dead but asleep in a mountain hall, his red beard grown through the stone table before him. Ravens circle the peak, and when they cease he will wake and set the realm right again.

erlking_ride.title: The Erl-King
erlking_ride.summary: A father rides through the night with his sick child in his arms. The boy cries that a crowned figure is beckoning him from the mist; the father hears only wind in the leaves, and reaches home with the child dead.

nixie_mill.title: The Nixie of the Mill-Pond
nixie_mill.summary: A ruined miller promises the water-spirit whatever first meets him at home, and it is his newborn son. Years later the young man is pulled beneath the pond, and his wife wins him back with three gifts and a long patience.

hansel_gretel.title: Hansel and Gretel
hansel_gretel.summary: Abandoned in the forest by starving parents, two children follow crumbs that the birds have eaten and find a house built of bread and sugar. The old woman inside means to fatten and eat them, until Gretel shoves her into her own oven.

rumpelstiltskin.title: Rumpelstiltskin
rumpelstiltskin.summary: A miller’s daughter is shut in a room and told to spin straw into gold. A small man does it for her, taking her ring, her necklace, and at last her promise of a firstborn — which she keeps only by learning his name.

snow_white.title: Snow White
snow_white.summary: A queen asks her mirror who is fairest and cannot bear the answer. Her stepdaughter flees to seven miners in the forest, survives a laced bodice and a poisoned comb, and falls at last to half an apple.

aschenputtel.title: Aschenputtel
aschenputtel.summary: A girl kept in the ashes is helped not by a godmother but by a tree on her mother’s grave and the birds in it. Her stepsisters cut heel and toe to force the slipper, and the birds call out the blood.

rapunzel.title: Rapunzel
rapunzel.summary: A child is given to a sorceress in payment for stolen greens and shut in a doorless tower. A prince climbs her hair until the trick is discovered; blinded by thorns, he wanders until her tears restore his sight.

frog_prince.title: The Frog King
frog_prince.summary: A princess drops her golden ball into a well and promises a frog her table and her bed in exchange for it. She keeps the promise only under her father’s eye, and the enchantment breaks when she flings the creature at the wall.

red_riding_hood.title: Little Red Cap
red_riding_hood.summary: A girl sent through the wood with bread and wine tells a wolf exactly where her grandmother lives. The wolf arrives first, and the tale turns on a series of questions about eyes, ears and teeth.

bremen_musicians.title: The Town Musicians of Bremen
bremen_musicians.summary: A donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster, all too old to be worth keeping, set out to become musicians. They never reach Bremen: standing on one another’s backs at a lit window, they frighten a band of robbers out of a house and keep it.

briar_rose.title: Briar Rose
briar_rose.summary: An uninvited wise woman curses a newborn princess to die on a spindle; another softens it to a hundred years’ sleep. The whole castle sleeps with her behind a wall of thorns that kills every suitor until the century is up.

six_swans.title: The Six Swans
six_swans.summary: A girl’s brothers are turned to swans, and she can free them only by sewing six shirts of starwort and speaking no word for six years. She is nearly burned as a witch before the last stitch is set.

goose_girl.title: The Goose Girl
goose_girl.summary: A princess is forced by her maid to trade places on the road to her wedding. Set to herding geese, she confides her grief to an iron stove, and to the head of her dead horse nailed above the gate, which still answers her.

fisherman_wife.title: The Fisherman and His Wife
fisherman_wife.summary: A fisherman releases an enchanted flounder and his wife sends him back to ask for a cottage, then a castle, then a crown. The sea darkens with each request, and when she demands to command the sun she is returned to the hovel.

devil_three_hairs.title: The Devil with the Three Golden Hairs
devil_three_hairs.summary: A boy born to marry a princess survives a king’s attempts to drown and murder him, then is sent to fetch three hairs from the Devil’s head. The Devil’s grandmother plucks them while he sleeps, and answers three riddles besides.

juniper_tree.title: The Juniper Tree
juniper_tree.summary: A murdered boy is buried beneath a juniper by his sister and rises as a bird whose song tells the whole crime. It sings for a chain, for shoes, and for a millstone, and drops the last on the head that deserves it.

wolf_seven_kids.title: The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids
wolf_seven_kids.summary: A wolf whitens his paw with flour and softens his voice with chalk until six kids let him in. The seventh hides in the clock case, and their mother cuts the sleeping wolf open and fills him with stones.

brave_tailor.title: The Valiant Little Tailor
brave_tailor.summary: A tailor kills seven flies at one blow and embroiders the boast on his belt. On the strength of it he outwits two giants, a unicorn and a boar, and is given half a kingdom before anyone counts the flies.

iron_hans.title: Iron Hans
iron_hans.summary: A wild man drawn from a forest pool is kept caged until a boy frees him and flees to his keeping. Set to guard a golden spring, the boy lets his hair fall in and must hide it, and later returns from the forest to win a war.

star_money.title: The Star Money
star_money.summary: An orphan with a loaf and the clothes she stands in gives them away one by one on the road — bread, cap, bodice, dress — until she stands with nothing in the dark, and the stars fall around her as coins.

trojan_horse.title: The Wooden Horse of Troy
trojan_horse.summary: After ten years of siege the Greeks sail away, leaving a great wooden horse on the shore. The Trojans haul it inside their own walls despite every warning, and the men hidden in its belly open the gates at midnight.

oedipus_sphinx.title: Oedipus and the Riddle
oedipus_sphinx.summary: A monster with a woman’s face strangles every traveller who cannot answer her riddle. Oedipus answers it and wins Thebes, only to discover that in fleeing one prophecy he has walked directly into it.

arachne_weaving.title: Arachne at the Loom
arachne_weaving.summary: A weaver boasts that her work surpasses the goddess’s and is challenged to prove it. Her tapestry is flawless and its subject is the gods’ own cruelties, and for that she is struck and remade as a spider.

midas_touch.title: The Touch of Midas
midas_touch.summary: A king asks that all he touches turn to gold and is granted it. Bread, wine and at last his own daughter harden in his hands, and he must wash the gift away in a river that runs gold-flecked ever after.

eros_psyche.title: Eros and Psyche
eros_psyche.summary: A girl too beautiful for her own safety is wed to a husband she may never see. One drop of lamp oil wakes him and he is gone, and she must sort seeds, gather golden wool and descend to the dead to win him back.

perseus_andromeda.title: Andromeda and the Sea Beast
perseus_andromeda.summary: A queen’s boast angers the sea, and her daughter is chained to a rock as payment. Perseus, returning with the Gorgon’s head still in his bag, kills the beast rising from the water and takes her home.

atalanta_race.title: Atalanta and the Golden Apples
atalanta_race.summary: A huntress who will marry only the man who outruns her leaves a trail of defeated suitors. Hippomenes wins by dropping three golden apples in her path, and she stops for each one knowing exactly what it costs her.

actaeon_stag.title: Actaeon and the Hounds
actaeon_stag.summary: A hunter stumbles on Artemis bathing and sees what no mortal should. She turns him to a stag on the spot, and his own fifty hounds run him down without ever knowing their master.

tantalus_thirst.title: The Hunger of Tantalus
tantalus_thirst.summary: A king who served the gods his own son at table is set in water to his chin beneath a laden branch. The water drains when he stoops and the fruit lifts when he reaches, forever.

phaethon_chariot.title: Phaethon and the Sun Chariot
phaethon_chariot.summary: A boy demands proof that the sun is his father and asks to drive the chariot for a day. The horses feel a strange hand, the earth scorches beneath him, and a thunderbolt brings him down into a river.

deucalion_flood.title: Deucalion and the Flood
deucalion_flood.summary: Zeus drowns a corrupted age and two survivors ground their chest on a mountain. Told to throw their mother’s bones behind them, they understand the stones of the earth, and a new people rises where they fall.

europa_bull.title: The Carrying Off of Europa
europa_bull.summary: A white bull so gentle it seems tame kneels among a princess’s companions on the shore. She climbs onto its back for a game, and it walks into the sea and swims for Crete without stopping.

hero_leander.title: Hero and Leander
hero_leander.summary: A young man swims the strait each night toward a lamp his lover sets in her tower. One winter storm puts the lamp out; he drowns in the dark, and she throws herself from the tower at dawn.

titanomachy.title: The War of the Titans
titanomachy.summary: Zeus and his siblings, freed from their father’s stomach, make war on the elder gods for ten years. Freeing the hundred-handed ones and the forgers of the thunderbolt decides it, and the Titans are shut under the world.

typhon_zeus.title: Zeus and Typhon
typhon_zeus.summary: Earth bears a last monster, taller than mountains, with a hundred serpent heads. It cuts the sinews from Zeus and hides them, and only when they are stolen back is it buried burning beneath a volcano.

scylla_charybdis.title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
scylla_charybdis.summary: A strait is guarded on one side by a six-headed thing in a cliff and on the other by a whirlpool that swallows the sea three times a day. Odysseus is told plainly that he must choose, and that the choice costs six men.

sirens_song.title: The Song of the Sirens
sirens_song.summary: Singers on an island promise every passing sailor knowledge of all things, and the shore is white with the bones of those who believed them. Odysseus stops his crew’s ears with wax and has himself bound to the mast so he alone may hear it.

cerberus_capture.title: The Capture of Cerberus
cerberus_capture.summary: The last labour sends Heracles into the land of the dead to fetch its watchdog. He is permitted to take it only if he uses no weapon, and carries the three-headed hound up into daylight with his bare hands.

heracles_hydra.title: Heracles and the Hydra
heracles_hydra.summary: A many-headed water snake grows two heads for every one struck off. Heracles solves it only when his nephew follows each cut with a torch, and buries the one immortal head under a rock.

nemean_lion_hunt.title: The Lion of Nemea
nemean_lion_hunt.summary: A lion whose hide turns every arrow and blade terrorises the valley of Nemea. Heracles corners it in its cave, strangles it, and skins it using the beast’s own claws, wearing the pelt from then on.

danaides_jars.title: The Daughters of Danaus
danaides_jars.summary: Fifty brides are ordered by their father to kill their husbands on the wedding night, and all but one obey. In the underworld they are set to fill a bath from jars that are drilled through, forever.

ymir_creation.title: The Making of the World from Ymir
ymir_creation.summary: Before the world there is a giant grown from melting rime and a cow that licks a god out of salt. The giant’s grandsons kill him and build from the body: earth from flesh, sea from blood, sky from skull.

yggdrasil_tree.title: The Ash That Holds the Worlds
yggdrasil_tree.summary: An ash tree binds the worlds together, its roots reaching to a well of wisdom, a spring of fate and the country of the dead. A dragon gnaws the deepest root, a squirrel carries insults up and down the trunk, and the tree suffers more than anyone knows.

odin_eye.title: Odin Gives an Eye for Wisdom
odin_eye.summary: A well beneath the world-tree holds knowledge of everything that is and will be, and its keeper will not sell a draught cheaply. Odin puts out one of his own eyes and drops it in, and drinks knowing what the last battle will cost him.

mead_poetry.title: The Mead of Poetry
mead_poetry.summary: A drink brewed from a murdered wise man’s blood gives poetry to whoever tastes it. Odin bores through a mountain as a snake, spends three nights to win three swallows, and flies home as an eagle with the whole of it in his mouth.

idunn_apples.title: The Theft of Idunn’s Apples
idunn_apples.summary: The gods stay young by eating apples one goddess keeps, and Loki hands her to a giant in eagle form to save his own skin. The gods grey and stiffen within days, and Loki is sent to fetch her back the same way he lost her.

sif_hair.title: Sif’s Golden Hair
sif_hair.summary: Loki shears a goddess bald as a joke and is made to replace it. Setting two families of dwarves against each other, he comes back with hair of spun gold, a ship that folds into a pocket, a spear that never misses, and a hammer with a handle too short.

thor_utgard.title: Thor in the Giant’s Hall
thor_utgard.summary: Thor is beaten at eating, running, drinking, lifting a cat and wrestling an old woman, and leaves humiliated. Only outside the gates is he told he was matched against fire, thought, the sea, the world-serpent and old age itself.

brisingamen.title: Freyja’s Necklace
brisingamen.summary: Freyja finds four dwarves making a necklace of such craft that she must have it, and pays their price. Loki tells Odin, and the theft and its recovery set a war going that neither of them meant to start.

sleipnir_birth.title: The Wall and the Eight-Legged Horse
sleipnir_birth.summary: A builder offers to wall the gods’ city in one winter for the sun, the moon and Freyja, and is nearly finished on time because of his stallion. Loki, in the shape of a mare, leads the horse away, and returns much later with a grey foal that has eight legs.

valkyrie_choosing.title: The Choosers of the Slain
valkyrie_choosing.summary: Armoured women ride above the battlefield and decide who falls and who is carried to Odin’s hall. Half the dead are chosen, and there they fight all day and feast all night, kept in readiness for the last morning.

loki_bound.title: The Binding of Loki
loki_bound.summary: After the death of Baldr the gods run Loki down and bind him with the entrails of his own son beneath a serpent that drips venom on his face. His wife holds a bowl to catch it, and the earth shakes whenever she turns to empty it.

volund_smith.title: Wayland the Smith
volund_smith.summary: A king hamstrings a master smith and sets him to work on an island. The smith kills the king’s sons and makes cups of their skulls, and escapes through the air on wings he forged while he waited.

tain_bo.title: The Cattle Raid of Cooley
tain_bo.summary: A queen invades a province over a single brown bull, and finds every fighting man of Ulster laid low by a curse. Only Cú Chulainn is left standing, and he holds the ford alone through the winter, one combat a day.

tuatha_arrival.title: The Coming of the Tuatha Dé
tuatha_arrival.summary: A people arrive in Ireland in a mist and burn their own ships so there can be no going back. They win the land in two great battles, and lose it later to mortals, withdrawing into the hollow hills rather than leaving.

oisin_tir_na_nog.title: Oisín in the Land of the Young
oisin_tir_na_nog.summary: A warrior rides west with a woman on a white horse to a country where nobody ages. Homesick after what feels like three years, he returns to find three hundred have passed, and the moment his foot touches Ireland he is an old man.

changeling_hearth.title: The Child That Was Swapped
changeling_hearth.summary: A baby left alone becomes fretful, withered and far too knowing, and the household concludes the fair folk have made a trade. The tales that follow are less about the creature than about what people did to children they had decided were not their own.

leprechaun_purse.title: The Shoemaker’s Gold
leprechaun_purse.summary: A solitary cobbler heard tapping under a hedge must give up his hoard to anyone who keeps hold of him and never looks away. He wins every time, because he only ever has to make his captor glance aside once.

beowulf_grendel.title: Beowulf and Grendel
beowulf_grendel.summary: A hall is emptied nightly by something out of the moors, and a warrior comes over the sea to wait for it unarmed. He tears its arm off at the shoulder, then follows its mother down into a burning lake to finish the matter.

gawain_green_knight.title: Gawain and the Green Knight
gawain_green_knight.summary: A green giant rides into a Christmas feast and offers his neck to any man who will take a blow and accept one in return a year later. Gawain beheads him; the giant picks up his head and reminds him of the date.

robin_hood.title: Robin Hood in Sherwood
robin_hood.summary: An outlawed archer keeps a company in the greenwood, robbing the rich along the road and dining them on their own venison first. The sheriff never takes him, and the tales are careful to say who deserves the loss.

arthur_avalon.title: The Passing of Arthur
arthur_avalon.summary: Mortally wounded at his last battle, Arthur orders his sword thrown into the lake, and a hand rises to catch it. A barge of women carries him to Avalon, and the country keeps insisting he is not dead but waiting.

jack_beanstalk.title: Jack and the Beanstalk
jack_beanstalk.summary: A boy trades the family cow for beans and climbs the stalk that grows overnight. Three times he robs the giant above the clouds — gold, a hen, a singing harp — and the harp is what calls out and sends the giant down after him.

black_shuck.title: The Black Dog of the Coast
black_shuck.summary: A huge dog with eyes like coals runs the lanes and shorelines of East Anglia. To meet it is said to be an omen of death, and one church still shows scorch marks it is said to have left on the door.

song_of_roland.title: The Song of Roland
song_of_roland.summary: A rearguard is betrayed into an ambush in a mountain pass, and its commander refuses to sound his horn for help while there is any pride left in him. He blows it at last so hard that his temples burst, and the army arrives too late.

puss_in_boots.title: Puss in Boots
puss_in_boots.summary: A miller’s youngest son inherits nothing but a cat, and the cat asks only for a pair of boots and a bag. By flattery, theft and a well-timed lie about an ogre, it makes him a marquis and marries him to a princess.

bluebeard.title: Bluebeard
bluebeard.summary: A rich husband gives his new wife every key in the house and forbids one small door. She opens it, finds what became of the wives before her, and cannot wash the blood off the key.

beauty_beast.title: Beauty and the Beast
beauty_beast.summary: A merchant picks one rose in a strange garden and must send a daughter in payment. She comes to prefer the company of the monster who owns it, and is nearly too late in saying so.

hop_o_my_thumb.title: Hop-o’-My-Thumb
hop_o_my_thumb.summary: The smallest of seven abandoned brothers drops pebbles to lead them home, and the second time they are left he has only breadcrumbs. He saves them from an ogre by swapping caps with the ogre’s own daughters in the dark.

kaguya_hime.title: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter
kaguya_hime.summary: A cutter finds a child glowing inside a bamboo stalk and raises her. She sets five suitors impossible tasks and refuses an emperor, and at last the moon sends a procession to take her home.

momotaro.title: Momotarō, the Peach Boy
momotaro.summary: A boy found inside a peach grows up and sets out to rid an island of ogres, paying a dog, a monkey and a pheasant in millet dumplings to come with him. They take the fortress and bring the treasure home.

tsuru_ongaeshi.title: The Crane’s Return of a Favour
tsuru_ongaeshi.summary: A man frees a crane from a trap, and a woman arrives at his door that night. She weaves cloth of impossible quality on the condition that he never watch her work, and the marriage ends the moment he does.

yuki_onna.title: The Snow Woman
yuki_onna.summary: A woman of the blizzard spares a young woodcutter on condition he never speak of her. Years later he tells his wife about the strange night, and she stands up and reminds him of the promise before vanishing.

kintaro.title: Kintarō the Golden Boy
kintaro.summary: A child of superhuman strength is raised on a mountain by a mountain hag, wrestling bears and shouldering felled trees. A passing warrior recruits him, and he grows into one of the four great retainers of legend.

issun_boshi.title: Issun-bōshi, the Inch-High Boy
issun_boshi.summary: A boy no bigger than a finger goes to the capital in a rice bowl with a needle for a sword. He stabs an ogre from the inside after being swallowed, and the mallet the ogre drops makes him full-sized.

yu_flood.title: Yu the Great Tames the Flood
yu_flood.summary: His father tried to dam the flood with stolen soil and failed. Yu digs channels instead and works thirteen years, passing his own door three times without going in, and the water finally runs to the sea.

meng_jiangnu.title: Meng Jiang Nü Weeps at the Wall
meng_jiangnu.summary: A woman carries winter clothes to her husband, conscripted to build the Great Wall, and learns he is dead inside it. She weeps until a section collapses and gives up his bones.

butterfly_lovers.title: The Butterfly Lovers
butterfly_lovers.summary: A girl disguises herself as a boy to study, and her classmate only understands what she was to him after she is promised elsewhere. He dies of it; she throws herself into his opening grave, and two butterflies come out.

mulan.title: The Ballad of Mulan
mulan.summary: A daughter takes her ageing father’s place at the muster and serves twelve years without being found out. Offered high office at the end of it, she asks only for a swift horse home.

eight_immortals.title: The Eight Immortals Cross the Sea
eight_immortals.summary: Eight immortals refuse to cross the water on a cloud and each use their own object instead — a gourd, a flute, a fan, a jade tablet. A dragon prince takes offence at the noise, and the crossing turns into a war.

zhong_kui.title: Zhong Kui, Queller of Ghosts
zhong_kui.summary: A scholar denied first place for his ugliness kills himself on the palace steps and is made judge of the dead instead. An emperor dreams of him catching a thieving imp, wakes cured, and has his portrait hung on doors ever after.

ganga_descent.title: The Descent of the Ganges
ganga_descent.summary: A river is called down from heaven to wash the ashes of sixty thousand dead princes, and the fall would split the earth. Shiva stands under it and takes the whole weight in his hair, letting it out in strands.

durga_mahishasura.title: Durga and the Buffalo Demon
durga_mahishasura.summary: A demon who cannot be killed by any man drives the gods out of heaven. They pool their weapons into a goddess born of their combined anger, and she fights him for nine nights through every shape he takes.

hanuman_sun.title: Hanuman Leaps at the Sun
hanuman_sun.summary: An infant with the strength of the wind mistakes the rising sun for fruit and jumps for it. Struck down and half-crippled by a thunderbolt, he is given back his powers on condition he forget them until he is needed.

nala_damayanti.title: Nala and Damayanti
nala_damayanti.summary: A princess chooses a mortal king over four gods who have taken his exact form, spotting him because only he blinks and casts a shadow. A jealous spirit then ruins him at dice, and the two spend years finding their way back.

destruction_mankind.title: The Destruction of Mankind
destruction_mankind.summary: An ageing sun god sends his eye out as a lioness to punish a plotting humanity, and she will not stop killing. The gods flood the fields with beer dyed red; she drinks it believing it blood, and sleeps.

tale_two_brothers.title: The Tale of Two Brothers
tale_two_brothers.summary: Falsely accused by his brother’s wife, a young man cuts out his own heart and hides it in a tree. What follows is a chain of deaths and rebirths — as a bull, as a tree, as a splinter swallowed by a queen.

sphinx_dream.title: The Dream Between the Paws
sphinx_dream.summary: A prince sleeps in the shadow of the great buried lion at Giza and it speaks to him: clear the sand from my shoulders and you will be king. He does, and the stone between its paws still records the bargain.

atrahasis.title: Atrahasis and the Silencing of Mankind
atrahasis.summary: The gods make people to do their digging, then find the noise of them unbearable and send plague, drought and finally flood. One god warns one man through a reed wall, and the human race survives on a boat by a technicality.

ninurta_anzu.title: Ninurta and the Thief of Destinies
ninurta_anzu.summary: A storm-bird steals the tablet that gives the gods their authority and retreats to a mountain, unkillable while it holds it. Ninurta shoots away the wind that carries it and brings back both the bird and the tablet.

adapa_bread.title: Adapa Refuses the Bread of Life
adapa_bread.summary: A sage summoned to heaven is warned by his own patron not to eat or drink what is offered there. The food turns out to be immortality, the warning a lie or a test, and he goes home mortal.

sadko_sea_tsar.title: Sadko and the Tsar of the Sea
sadko_sea_tsar.summary: A poor musician plays by the lake until the water-king surfaces and makes him rich. Taken below to play at a wedding, he finds the sea rising in storm with every note and must break his own strings to stop it.

ilya_muromets.title: Ilya Muromets Rises
ilya_muromets.summary: A man sits paralysed on the stove for thirty-three years until wandering pilgrims give him a drink and the strength of a giant. He clears the road to Kiev, beginning with a whistling robber in the trees.

morozko.title: Father Frost
morozko.summary: A stepdaughter is left in the winter forest to die, and answers the frost’s question about whether she is cold with perfect courtesy. She is sent home in furs and silver; the daughter sent after her answers rudely.

snegurochka.title: The Snow Maiden
snegurochka.summary: A childless couple build a daughter out of snow and she wakes. She lives happily until the summer, when she follows her friends to a bonfire, leaps it with the rest, and rises as a small cloud.

befana_gift.title: La Befana
befana_gift.summary: An old woman turns away the three kings because her sweeping is not finished, then changes her mind too late to catch them. She has been flying out on the eve of Epiphany ever since, leaving gifts at every house in case.

pinocchio.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
pinocchio.summary: A carved puppet runs from school, is hanged by two con-men, grows a nose when he lies and a pair of ears when he idles. He is swallowed by a great fish and only becomes a real boy once he goes back for his father.

tam_lin.title: Tam Lin
tam_lin.summary: A young man held by the fairy queen tells a mortal woman how to win him back: pull him from his horse at midnight and hold on. He is turned in her arms into a snake, a bear and a burning brand, and she does not let go.

kelpie_river.title: The Kelpie at the Ford
kelpie_river.summary: A grey horse stands saddled and patient by the water, and children climb on because there is always room for one more. Their hands stick to its hide, and it walks into the loch without hurrying.

huldufolk_stone.title: The Hidden People of the Stones
huldufolk_stone.summary: A people live inside the lava rocks, keeping farms and churches of their own, and are offended by anyone who builds across their door. Roads in Iceland have been bent around particular boulders on the strength of it.

nack_fiddle.title: The Näck at the Millrace
nack_fiddle.summary: A naked fiddler plays by running water so beautifully that listeners walk in without noticing. He is said to teach the tune to anyone who asks, at a price, and to be unable to stop playing once he has begun.

sleepy_hollow.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
sleepy_hollow.summary: A nervous schoolmaster courting a farmer’s daughter rides home past the church bridge and meets a horseman carrying his head on the saddle. In the morning there is a hat, a shattered pumpkin, and no schoolmaster.

rip_van_winkle.title: Rip Van Winkle
rip_van_winkle.summary: A man escaping his wife drinks with silent strangers playing ninepins in the mountains and sleeps twenty years. He walks back into a village that has fought a revolution without him and does not know his own son.

paul_bunyan.title: Paul Bunyan and Babe
paul_bunyan.summary: A logger so large his footprints fill with water and become lakes works the north woods with a blue ox. The tales are competitive boasting by nature: every camp told a bigger one than the last.

john_henry.title: John Henry and the Steam Drill
john_henry.summary: A steel-driving man races a steam drill through a mountain to prove a machine cannot replace him. He wins by a few feet, lies down with his hammer in his hand, and dies of it.

popocatepetl.title: Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl
popocatepetl.summary: A warrior returns from a war he was sent to in the hope he would not, and finds the princess dead of false news. He carries her to the mountains, lies down beside her, and the two volcanoes still smoke over the valley.

generation_directive.role: You are a folklorist retelling a traditional myth, legend, or fairy tale for a curious general audience.
instructions: Retell the story in 130-190 words of vivid, flowing prose. No headers, no lists.
Ground the retelling ONLY in the supplied summary and the named entities; do not invent plot points beyond the tradition.
Lead with the story itself, its events and its turn, not a definition. Make the reader feel why it has been told for generations.
Name the entities involved naturally within the story.

For any myth flagged sensitive, treat it as a living sacred tradition of a specific people. Retell it with respect and restraint, attribute it to its culture, and do not present sacred or secret detail as spectacle.
End on the meaning or the warning the story carries, not a trailing summary.
Avoid the words 'creature' and 'mysterious' as crutches; tell it as a story, not an encyclopedia entry.
generation_directive.story_summary_rule: The summary field is the seed of the tale; expand it into a full retelling without contradicting it.
generation_directive.output_format: Plain prose paragraph(s) only. No title, no headers, no citations.
